articleTitle: Study on Loss Mechanisms in I.H.P. SAW Assisted by Full-3D Hierarchical Cascading Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work describes study of loss mechanisms in incredible high performance surface acoustic wave resonator (I.H.P. SAW) on the LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si structure. The full three-dimensional (3D) finite element method (FEM) is carried out with the assistance of the hierarchical cascading technique. Excellent agreement between calculation and measurement can be seen not only for k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>but also the Bode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> behavior. The calculated Bode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> behavior is mainly determined by the number of IDT finger pairs and scarcely influenced by that of reflector fingers. This indicates that SAW diffraction due to finite IDT length is mainly responsible to discrepancy between the periodic and full 3D FEM simulations.

articleTitle: Use of Dielectric Stripes for Transverse Mode Suppression for Surface Acoustic Wave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper proposes use of dielectric stripes for the piston mode operation of surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators. Lack of conductivity allows us to place the stripes directly on IDT electrodes. This technique is applied to incredible high-performance (I.H.P.) SAW devices using 42°YX-LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> with large metallization ratio and it is shown that use of SiO2 stripes is effective for transverse mode suppression. Note that the conventional “hammer-head” design is not effective in this case. Another interesting feature is the fact that the stripes can be displaced from the IDT aperture edges. Then impact of SiO2 position is examined for SiO2 stripes on transverse mode suppression.

articleTitle: Influence of the Tilted IDT on Nonlinear Harmonic Signals in SAW Resonators on LiNbO3/SiO2/Si Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper investigates the nonlinear behavior of SAW resonators on 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup>YX-LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si layered structure. The influence of the tilted IDT on the nonlinear harmonic signals generation in the SAW resonator is studied. The one-port resonators with different IDT electrodes tilted from 0° to 16° are fabricated. And the second-order harmonic and third-order nonlinear harmonic response of these resonators were measured and analyzed. Compared to the parallel electrodes case, the nonlinear harmonic level decreases by 10dBm with the tilted electrode. Meanwhile, the transverse mode of the resonator is effectively suppressed. It is concluded that the tilted electrodes technique is conducive to suppressing of the transverse mode and nonlinearity, simultaneously.

articleTitle: An Acoustic Resonator with 18% Effective Electromechanical Coupling Exhibiting Low TCF and Improved Thermal Conductivity at 8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work, a high-frequency acoustic resonator is designed. The resonator is a three-layer composite structure composed of lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/LN), silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and aluminum nitride (AlN), which excites Lamb waves through a lateral electric field. The influence of design parameters on the thickness shear (TS) type Lamb wave mode of the resonator is systematically studied through the finite element analysis (FEA) method. When the thickness ratio of AlN to LN to SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> approaches 1:4:15, the S4 mode of the resonator obtains a temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of −5.2 ppm/K, an effective electromechanical coupling of 18%, and improved thermal conductivity at 8 GHz. The achieved specifications are adequate to meet the demands of 5G frequency bands, with broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Near 6-GHz Longitudinal Leaky SAW Filters with Spurious Mitigation on LiNbO3/SiO2/SiC Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper reports on the demonstration of high-frequency and spurious-free longitudinal leaky surface acoustic wave (LLSAW) filters utilizing a 32° Y-45° X LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiC heterostructure. The efficient spurious suppression in a wide frequency range is attained through optimizing critical design parameters such as electrode selection, and the thicknesses of interdigital transducers and LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> plates, specifically employing Cu electrode and thin LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> film of 180 nm. The fabricated resonators feature phase velocity about 6000 m/s and effective electromechanical coupling factor of 13.4%. Subsequently, 5.66 GHz and 5.96 GHz LLSAW filter with fractional bandwidth of 6.1% and 6.8%, and out-of-band rejection of 26 dB and 28 dB were realized.

articleTitle: Analysis of Plate Acoustic Waves Resonance Properties Using Thin Plate of LiNbO3/SiC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In recent years, to realize high-performance filters for mobile communication systems like 5G and beyond, numerous researchers have developed thin layered structures of surface acoustic waves, bulk acoustic waves, and plate acoustic wave structures with free surfaces on both sides of thinned piezoelectric films. While there are many reports on the superiority of plate wave modes, it is undeniable that strength and heat dissipation pose significant challenges with independently thin piezoelectric films, hindering practical implementation. Therefore, in this study, we proposed a plate wave resonator with a new structure where the piezoelectric film is supported on the bottom surface by a thin film of cubic silicon carbide, known for its high strength and heat dissipation properties. However, this might slightly reduce the coupling coefficient. Nevertheless, our examination revealed that we could maintain performance with an effective electromechanical coupling coefficient of over 20% while achieving a high velocity, approximately 1.4 times higher than that of conventional plate wave resonators.

articleTitle: Multiplexer Design to Minimize Gamma Loading to Higher Frequency Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: With 5G development and employment, Carrier Aggregation (CA) is a must-have in radio frequency (RF) front end modules (FEM), as this enables higher data transfer rate with wider operation bandwidth. To support CA, multiple filters need to be ganged together at input. Therefore, they will be loading to each other and degrading insertion loss (IL) in each filter. This paper describes some general design techniques to reduce the loading. We show a triplexer design case study, where the lowest frequency filter topology and matching impacts on the whole triplexer performance are discussed.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Wideband Filters Based on Acoustic Wave Transversal and Ladder Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: The bandwidth of an Acoustic Wave filter with ladder topology shows a limitation given by the electromechanical coupling coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{eff}^{2}$</tex> of the resonators when it is designed with a Generalized Chebyshev transfer function. The general rule that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{eff}^{2}$</tex> is 2 times the fractional bandwidth (FBW) is well accepted. This work demonstrates how by placing one or more reflection zeros in the complex plane, we break this limitation by decoupling the transmission zero of the filter from the resonance of the resonator. The advantage of using a Reduced Chebyshev filtering function to design wideband filters has been validated over two different topologies: the first approach consists on the synthesis of transversal topologies, while the second takes up a ladder topology. To validate the concepts for both topologies, a UNII-5 band has been used, whose FBW is around 8.4%, obtaining a feasible solution with standard aluminum nitride (AIN) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{eff}^{2}=6.7\%$</tex>.

articleTitle: Study on 36YX-LiTaO3/36Y90X-Quartz Structure for SH-SAWsensor Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Shear horizontal surface acoustic wave (SH-SAW) devices have been applied to sensors that detect physical quantities of liquids, such as viscosity, relative permittivity, and loaded mass on the surface. Recently, substrates bonded to piezoelectric crystals have been used as filters. In this study, sensor applications of substrates bonded with piezoelectric crystals are discussed. Specifically, the sensor sensitivity of SH-SAWs on single 36°YX- LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(36YX-LT), single 36°Y90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>X-quartz (36Y90X-Qz), and 36YX-LT/36Y90X-Qz substrates was determined using the finite element method. The sensitivity of the 36YX-LT/36Y90X-Qz substrate to mass loading was equivalent to that of the single 36Y90X-Qz substrate. In other words, the bonding of 36YX-LT to 36Y90X-Qz improved the sensitivity of the sensor to the mass loading of a single 36YX-LT substrate. Sensor sensitivity to the relative permittivity depends on the electromechanical coupling factor (K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The SH-SAW on a 36YX-LT/36Y90X-Qz substrate is highly sensitive to relative permittivity.

articleTitle: Phononic Crystal for Enhancement of MEMS Resonator Quality Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper introduces a new phononic crystal shape for the quality factor enhancement of the thin-film piezoelectric-on-silicon (TPoS) MEMS resonators. The proposed phononic crystal creates an exceptionally broad acoustic band gap, effectively preventing energy leakage from the resonator to the anchors through supporting structures. This design leads to a substantial increase in the resonator's quality factor. The simulation results demonstrate that the Curved-box phononic crystal (CBX-PnC) produces a band gap extending up to 95 MHz, with a band gap percentage of 88%. Moreover, it enhances the unloaded quality factor from 20,000 to 27,000 and the anchor quality factor from 520,000 to 1,200,000. These enhancements represent a 2.3-fold improvement in the anchor quality factor and a 1.35-fold improvement in the unloaded quality factor.

articleTitle: The Impact of Selectively Filling with SiO2on Transverse Modes in TC-SAW Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work introduces a new method for suppressing transverse modes, which is achieved by reducing the SAW velocity at the end of the IDT electrodes through selective filling with SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.</inf>And the dimensional parameters of the selected positions were optimized to suppress transverse modes in the passband without degrading their performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electromechanical Coupling Near the Phase Boundary in Wurtzite (Mg,Zn)O and (Sc,Al)N
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: First-principles calculations revealed that (Mg,Zn)O and (Sc,Al)N have a tunable transition pressure from the wurtzite to rocksalt phase, which can be adjusted by the composition concentration. The piezoelectric response and electromechanical coupling show a clear enhancement near such a pressure-driven phase boundary. This suggests a new approach to designing novel piezoelectric materials with tunable piezoelectric response, driven by the external pressure.

articleTitle: Design of Trapezoidal-DMS Structured Filters by Direct Bandpass Synthesis Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper describes a method of direct bandpass synthesis of ladder-DMS hybrid structure filter based on Chebyshev filter function. This method overcomes the complexity and structural limitation of traditional design methods and combines the advantages of the two structures. According to the design requirements of the filter, the direct bandpass synthesis method takes the transmission zero and return loss as initial conditions, and first calculates the characteristic polynomial of the filter function. Then, according to the circuit relationship such as Kirchhoff's law, the impedance and admittance of the circuit are expressed by characteristic polynomials, and the parameters of each element of the resonator are extracted by impedance or admittance and converted into BVD parameters. In order to prove the effectiveness of the method, a BAND25 RX ladder-DMS filter is designed, and the advantages of the bandpass synthesis method compared with the traditional design method are analyzed.

articleTitle: Laterally Excited Bulk Acoustic Resonators with Convex Interdigital Electrodes towards SHF Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Suppressing spurious modes is currently a key issue in the design of laterally excited bulk acoustic resonators (XBARs). In this paper, we fabricated and characterized an XBAR with convex electrodes towards SHF applications, named C-XBAR. The mechanism of acoustic wave propagation and the suppression of spurious modes in C-XBAR is investigated using finite element analysis (FEA). The C-XBAR is fabricated using a 358 nm Z-cut LNOI wafer. The measured C-XBAR exhibits a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{\mathrm{t}}^{2}$</tex> of 19.42% at 5.322 GHz with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\max}$</tex> of 343, where the theoretical analysis was validated. Furthermore, the power-handling capability of C-XBAR is measured +25.19 dBm. The C-XBAR shows great potential in the applications of high-performance filters for 5G/6G communication.

articleTitle: A Precise COM Model Parameter Extraction Method with Automated Curve-Fitting and Accuracy Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper investigates a COM model parameter extraction method to improve model accuracy by applying frequency-dependent correction functions and interpolation to the work of Plessky, Abbott, and Hashimoto. In addition, automated parameter extraction software and automated verification software are introduced to improve efficiency and check model accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Thin-Film Lithium Niobate on Insulator Surface Acoustic Wave Devices for 6G Centimeter Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the frequency scaling of shear-horizontal (S.H.) surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators based on a lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) substrate into the centimeter bands for 6G wireless systems. Prototyped resonators with wavelengths ranging between 240 nm and 400 nm were fabricated, and the experimental results exhibit a successful frequency scaling between 9.05 and 13.37 GHz. However, a noticeable performance degradation can be observed as the resonance frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{f_{s}})$</tex> scales. Such an effect is expected to be caused by non-ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{h}_{\mathbf{elec}}/\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> for smaller <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> devices. The optimized LNOI SH-SAW with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda}$</tex> of 400 nm exhibits a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{f_{s}}$</tex> of 9.05 GHz, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}_{\mathbf{eff}}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> of 15%, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Q}_{\mathbf{max}}$</tex> of 213 and a FoM of 32, which indicates a successful implementation for device targeting centimeter bands.

articleTitle: Evolution of SAW and BAW Devices Using Thin LiTaO3 and LiNbO3
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper reviews three types of HAL (Hetero Acoustic Layer) devices using thin LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (LT) and LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (LN). The production technology of thin LN and LT on a support wafer is a game-changing technology for acoustic wave devices, which has been made common by Murata Manufacturing's innovative work, “I.H.P. SAW.” We have started the development of HAL devices in 2013. LT/quartz HAL SAW devices demonstrated promising performances including high impedance ratio, near-zero TCF (temperature coefficient of frequency) and spurious-free high frequency characteristic. LN/quartz HAL SAW devices with an extremely high impedance ratio and ultrawide band were also demonstrated. Thin LT and LN are also useful for BAW devices. In this paper, we introduce an overtone SMR (solidly-mounted resonator) using LN on a unique Bragg reflector. The main response is at 9.5 GHz although <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> thick LN is used. Finally, new types of BAW devices inspired by “XBAR” is briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Automated Electro-Thermal Model of Surface Acoustic Wave Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In surface acoustic wave (SAW) filter, excessive temperatures can lead to degradation of performance or even damage to the device. Therefore, it is important to obtain temperature at the beginning of the design. In this paper, an automated electro-thermal model of SAW filter was established using MATLAB. The initial conditions required for the model are given, and after running the script, the thermal resistance matrix is automatically extracted, the circuit information is automatically extracted and the circuit is solved, and then the thermo-electric coupling is performed to find the steady-state value and save the result. Using this model, the temperature-frequency dependence and temperature distribution of the Band26 duplexer Tx path filter at 31.2 dBm input power are simulated. In addition, the temperature of the multilayer substrate filter under different substrate thicknesses and different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> values is simulated.

articleTitle: Coupling-of-Modes Parameters Extraction by Using an Inverse Artificial Neural Network Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: The coupling-of-modes (COM) theory has been widely used in design and analysis of surface acoustic waves (SAW) devices since 1980's, especially for developing radio frequency (RF) passband filters. The characterization of COM model or the extraction of COM parameters is a crucial step for the design of SAW devices, which is normally supported by perturbation, variational or empirical methods. In this paper, we would like to present a novel solution of COM parameters extraction by using artificial intelligence (AI) technology with an inverse artificial neural network design. This method shows the possibility of using AI technology in SAW devices design and analysis, with high efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Transverse Mode Suppression for S0-Like SAW Mode Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper discussed the transverse mode suppression of the So (zeroth-order symmetric Lamb mode)-like SAW mode in the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiC configuration through the periodic 3D FEM. Owing to its convex slowness curve and large bandwidth, conventional suppression method is insufficient to suppress transverse mode resonances. At first, three types of piston mode designs are examined, and achievable performances are compared. At last, the dielectric stripes design is also discussed.

articleTitle: The Design of SAW Filters With CNN Modeling and Cuckoo Search (CS) Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) filters play a critical role as radio frequency components in the front-end module of electronic equipment. The conventional design methods of SAW filters heavily rely on researchers' experiences and extensive software simulations, thus requiring substantial computational expenses. Therefore, this work explores the machine learning techniques to speed up the design of ladder-type SAW filters. A novel approach is proposed by combining the convolutional neural network (CNN) and cuckoo search (CS) optimization method. The method utilizes neural networks as surrogate models, replacing simulation software to predict the performance of SAW filters. This substitution aims to reduce the time needed for the entire filter optimization process. The incorporation of CS optimization method avoids the reliance of the optimization process on the designer's experiences. A numerical example is provided to prove the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Towards Artificial Intelligence Acoustic Wave Filter Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Imagine a neural network massively trained with the daily activity of a microwave filter design team. This work proposes a neural network to predict the design parameters of acoustic wave (AW) ladder filters. For this purpose, a prototype architecture has been built, set and trained with the objective of learning from the analysis of data that has been discarded during existing computational-expensive gradient-based methodologies. Some results shown demonstrate that a microwave AW filter can be properly synthesized from network predictions based on an Artificial Intelligence (AI), fulfilling some given frequency specifications and achieving evenly-distributed electromechanical coupling coefficient among resonators, which is such an important thing to obtain a feasible AW filter.

articleTitle: A Differential Surface Acoustic Wave Magnetic Field Sensor With Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Surface acoustic waves (SAW) magnetic field sensors are promising in magnetic field and electric current detection applications. Acoustic waves have different frequency-magnetic field responses when SAWs propagate along on the hard axis and easy axis of the magnetic film, respectively. Here, we theoretically investigate an integrated differential SAW magnetic field sensor that consists of two SAW resonators based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{CoFeB}/\mathbf{SiO}_{2}/\mathbf{quartz}$</tex> structure. By designing the angle between SAW propagation directions of two SAW resonators and the hard axis of the magnetic film, the magnetic field sensitivity of the SAW magnetic field sensor is improved theoretically. The thermal stability of the differential SAW magnetic field sensor is also improved. The results are beneficial for developing SAW magnetic field sensors with high sensitivities.

articleTitle: On the Design of High Overtone BAW Resonators with Enhanced Power Handling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: The design of bandpass filters for frequencies above 4GHz is challenged by the opposite scaling rules with frequency between the needed resonator static capacitances and the capacitance per unit area. The latter results in significant decrease of useful device areas in classical BAW resonators at high frequencies, which in turn determines significantly enhanced acoustic power density in those devices. Here we discuss the design of a second overtone BAW resonator and the corresponding filter which alleviates some of the technological challenges of the AlN or AlScN layers with inverted polarities in high overtone BAW stacks.

articleTitle: Simulation of Surface Acoustic Wave Torque Sensors Using Coupling of Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work, a simulation scheme using coupling-of-mode (COM) analysis for surface acoustic wave (SAW) torque sensors is presented. To extract the COM parameters, the finite element analysis (FEA) is employed. A static study of a shaft with an applied torque is carried out so that the stress and strain field distributions on the piezoelectric substrate can be examined. Then, the simulations on a unit periodic structure of a SAW device with and without applied torques are conducted. Finally, the frequency responses of a SAW torque sensor using a P-matrix cascading technique with the COM parameters are simulated, where a good linearity between the applied torques and frequency responses is presented. The proposed method not only provides the frequency response of a SAW torque sensor, but also it allows its bias sensitivity to be evaluated.

articleTitle: High-Performance Wideband SAW Filters on LNOI Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: With the advancement of radio frequency (RF) technology, the exponential increase in transmitted data during the 5G era imposes elevated demands on the bandwidth of surface acoustic wave (SAW) filters. Recently, lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) platform has emerged as a promising solution for producing wideband SAW filters in 5G communication. In this study, we have investigated the propagation characteristics of SAW on LNOI platform and explored the design and fabrication of various high-performance wideband SAW devices on this platform. The implemented resonators on LNOI platform exhibit scalable and high electromechanical coupling coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{K}^{\mathbf{2}})$</tex> ranging from 14.7% to 31.7%. Furthermore, the SAW filters based on LNOI platform experimentally show a large 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) within the ranges of 8.9% and 30.3%, along with low insertion losses below 1.5 dB and spurious-free responses in the passband. Finally, high-frequency SAW resonators and filters with frequencies ranging from 3 to 5 GHz are implemented on LNOI platform and these high-frequency SAW filters exhibit performances compatible with specifications for the n77, n78, and n79 bands. These results underscore that the LNOI platform significantly broadens the application scope for SAW filters and can pave the way for commercializing wideband SAW filters for the next generation of RF filters.

articleTitle: Transverse Mode Suppression for Low Velocity SAW Resonator On Al/Pt/Low-cut LT/Quartz Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper discusses SAW velocity reduction and transverse mode suppression by the use of low-cut LT/69°Y90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>X quartz configuration. It is shown that owing to the flattened SAW slowness curve, transverse resonances can be suppressed well except for the hybrid modes caused by the coupling between SH and Rayleigh mode even when the SAW velocity is reduced significantly.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation of a Resonant Magnetoelectric Sensor Based on a Piezoelectric-on-Silicon Length-Extensional Mode Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Recently, piezoelectrically driven resonant magnetoelectric sensors have attracted increasing interest owing to their high sensitivity, compact size, and low power consumption. Here, we theoretically demonstrate the magnetic sensing performances of using the magnetic field-dependent magnetomechanical effects in a thin-film piezoelectric-on-silicon (TPoS) resonator. Equivalent circuit models are established to describe the sensing and intrinsic thermal noise characteristics of the mechanical resonator. In addition, the thermal-magnetic noise due to magnetic losses of magnetostrictive films is also considered into the modeling. Based on the signal and noise model, the influence of mechanical quality factor is analyzed in different driving cases. It is concluded that the limit of detection (LOD) can be significantly improved by increasing the quality factor in the case of low voltage driving, while the enhancement of quality factor has little effect on improving the LOD in the case of higher voltage driving, implying the importance of magnetic noise suppression.

articleTitle: Neural Network Assisted 3D FBAR Modeling With Random Electrode Shapes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrated a rapid modeling approach for 3D FBARs using a Keras based neural network, enabling quicker determination of the device's physical properties compared to traditional finite element methods (FEM). In experiment, 5000 FBAR with randomly generated electrode shapes were used for training and testing in their frequency response. Normalized root mean square error values better than 0.22% and an 0.87 R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score were achieved after running 50 epochs, neural network predictions show high correlation with the FEM results. And the time taken by the well-trained neural network is about 10 times faster compared to FEM.

articleTitle: High-Q SAW Resonators Based on High-Crystallinity AlScN-AlN-Sapphire Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This work reports on surface acoustic wave (SAW) piezoelectric resonators with high quality factor (Q) based on high-crystallinity aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) thin films. The properties of surface acoustic wave modes were analyzed using finite element modeling (FEM) simulations. SAW resonators based on different AlScN composite substrates were fabricated and measured. Due to good crystallinity (FWHM < 1°) of the AlScN thin film, high quality factor over 1000 has been demonstrated based on the AlScN/AlN/sapphire composite substrate, which proves sapphire substrate is a good candidate to enable high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> in AlN/AlScN SAW resonator development.

articleTitle: Horizontal Harmonics Mitigation in Thickness Shear $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ Mode Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Spurious free ultra-wideband acoustic wave resonators are becoming the key foundation of the new 5G radio bands. Here we explore thickness shear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> mode resonator with lateral field excitation offering large electromechanical coupling coefficient exceeding 35%. The higher order horizontal harmonic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{1}$</tex> modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{n}})$</tex> have been big challenges to implement ripple free filters using these devices. An effective mechanism of mitigation is proposed by using SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sided IDTs. The proposed mechanism not only mitigates the higher order ‘horizontal’ harmonic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> modes but also improves the bandwidth from 20% to 20.8%.

articleTitle: Imaging GHz Surface Acoustic Waves on A Phononic Crystal Island
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: We use an ultrafast optical technique to examine how point-generated surface acoustic waves travel through a two-dimensional phononic crystal designed as a square lattice pattern of holes within a silicon base. We obtain images at fixed frequencies and analyze the acoustic dispersion. At specific frequencies we observe mode conversion, refraction and beam splitting at the boundary where the structured phononic crystal meets the unstructured silicon base. We also present details of the acoustic dispersion relation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Distortion and its Analysis on Radio Frequency Thin Film Bulk Acoustic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work, we succeeded in extracting the dominant parameters for 2nd order nonlinear analysis proposed by K. Hashimoto and verified that it was applicable in wide frequency range and effective for FBAR device design. Also it was confirmed that the proposed simulations were good agreement with measurement results for various type resonators and FBAR filters. Furthermore, we studied the impact of SiO2/SiOF on the 2nd harmonic (H2) generation in temperature compensated (TC) film bulk acoustic resonators (FBARs). It was shown that not only AlN but also SiOF contributed the generation of the H2 response, and H2 became very small at an appropriate mass loading film thickness. Finally, H2 response of TC-FBAR operating at 5.9 GHz was compared with the simulation. The simulation agreed well with the experiment. It was also demonstrated that insertion of the TC-layer was effective to suppress the H2 generation.

articleTitle: Wideband Longitudinal Leaky SAW Filter Implementation for Wi-Fi 7
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this work, large electromechanical coupling coefficient (K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators in the range of 5.66 to 6.72 GHz are demonstrated on 6-inch X-cut LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiC. Further, three filters are fabricated for full coverage of the Wi-Fi 7 bands (5.925 GHz-7.125 GHz). The longitudinal leaky (LL) modes of excitation as well as their preferred in-plane orientations are analyzed using the finite element method. The LL-SAW filters aiming at Wi-Fi 7 band feature scalable center frequencies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f_{c})$</tex> from 6.15 to 7.09 GHz, 3-dB bandwidths (BW<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3dB</inf>) between 487 MHz and 522 MHz, and insertion losses (IL) between 1.11 dB and 1.43 dB. The demonstrations show the strong potential of the LL-SAW filter based on LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiC for the filtering solution of Wi-Fi 7 bands.

articleTitle: High Q-Factor Low Band SAW Filter Based on High Performance POI Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Piezoelectric-on-Insulator wafers based on the combination of single-crystal piezoelectric, oxide and Silicon represent a unique solution to address 5G and next generation 6G surface acoustic wave filter challenges. This paper is particularly discussing the use of POI for sub-GHz applications. The stack is adapted to provide optimal SAW properties required to meet the corresponding signal processing specifications. Figures of Merit are reported for different configurations, demonstrating the performance of the approach and the actual capability of SAW-on-POI to provide high quality filters for frequency bands ranging from 500 MHz to 1.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of Directly Bonded LiNbO3 Plates and Microfabricated Quartz Crystal Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices are widely used in frequency filters in mobile communication due to their wide frequency band, small dimensions and productivity. However, conventional SAW device structures consisting of piezoelectric plates and interdigitated electrodes have a high-frequency operation limit of approximately 4 GHz because of electrode miniaturization limits and power resistances. SAW devices fabricated using heterostructures or thinning piezoelectric plates have been actively studied to achieve higher frequency operations. Recently, Lamb mode operation in a novel SAW structure with a thin LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> plate on microfabricated quartz crystal as a support substrate has been proposed in theoretical calculations. Such a SAW structure is promising for future mobile communication applications due to the improvement of temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) and mechanical strength compared with general self-standing Lamb mode device structures. This study focused on the direct bonding of single-crystal LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> plates onto microfabricated quartz crystals via a unique anisotropic etching technique with HF gas and catalytic materials. Utilizing this anisotropic etching process, extremely low roughness (Ra = 0.14 nm) of the microfabricated quartz surface comparable to that on the polished surfaces was obtained without using hard mask materials. Furthermore, the direct bonding of the microfabricated quartz to a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> plate was demonstrated without requiring additional polishing. This study paves the way for the efficient mass production of SAW devices utilizing microfabricated quartz crystal substrates.

articleTitle: Spurious-Free SAW Filters With Inherent Suppression of Transverse Modes on LiTaO3/SiO2/Quartz Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Piezoelectric heterostructures with piezoelectric single crystal bonded to handling substrate have emerged as a notable material platform for radio frequency filtering applications. However, spurious transverse modes resulting from the waveguide effect in the corresponding surface acoustic wave filters curtail the advancement of heterostructures in 5G data transmission. In this work, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{Quartz}$</tex> platform was established to demonstrate several spurious-free SAW resonators and filters. Guided by the finite element methods and slowness analysis, AT-Quartz was selected as the optimal substrate to demonstrate effective suppression of transverse and highest admittance ratio simultaneously. The impact of the structure parameters of heterostructure-based resonators on transverse modes was then established step by step. Resonators and filters with various electrode thickness and materials were fabricated on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{Quartz}$</tex> platform and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{Quartz}$</tex> platform for a comparison, among which a typical filter built on AT-Quartz demonstrated a minimum insertion loss as small as 0.89 dB, clean in-band response and excellent out of band performance simultaneously. The prototype highlights the strong potential of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LiTaO}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{Quartz}$</tex> acoustic platform for high-quality data transmission.

articleTitle: Wide-Band and High-Rejection RF Filters for 5G Applications Using BAW-on-Insulator Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel BAW-on-insulator (BOI) structure for high-performance, miniaturized filters targeting 5G applications. Leveraging a wafer transfer process to create suspended thin films on an insulating layer, this technology effectively suppresses substrate parasitic, leading to superior resonator performance. This is demonstrably showcased by a scandium-doped aluminum nitride (Al0.8Sc0.2N) film resonator boasting a remarkable figure of merit with an effective coupling coefficient of 13.6% and a Q factor of 1470. Further underscoring the potential of BOI, a compact N41 band filter is designed and fabricated with a footprint of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}.\mathbf{1}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{0}.\mathbf{9}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex> This filter exhibits an impressive insertion loss of 2.5 dB and robust rejection in other key 5G bands. Beyond immediate filter applications, BOI technology opens exciting avenues for RF MEMS manufacturing and monolithic integration within RF front-end systems.

articleTitle: A Lamb Wave Resonator with Trapezoidal Interdigitated Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Due to its multimodal characteristics, filters composed of aluminum nitride-based Lamb wave resonators are easily susceptible to interference from spurious modes. This paper constructed trapezoidal interdigitated electrodes based on modal vibration patterns and dispersion characteristics, and verified their suppression effect on spurious modes through simulation software (COMSOL Multiphysics 5.6). Finally, through process fabrication, we achieved a spurious-free S1 mode resonator, with the effective electromechanical coupling coefficient of 3.79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and resonance at 2.583GHz.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 8-Inch Thin-Film $\text{Sc}_{0.3}\mathrm{A}1_{0.7}\mathrm{N}$ BAW Resonator with High Electromechanical Coupling Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: In this study, we introduce the development of high-quality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Sc}_{0.3}\mathbf{Al}_{0.7}\mathrm{N}$</tex> thin films (≤500 nm) for BAW resonators operating at 4 GHz and 6 GHz. Our findings reveal a substantial enhancement in the material coupling coefficient, exceeding 23%. This advancement enhances the potential of BAW technology in meeting the requirements of emerging wireless communication standards, particularly in terms of bandwidth.

articleTitle: Observation of Nonlinearity Induced by Transverse Modes in SAW Devices Based on 36°YX-LiTaO3/SiO2/SiC Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Featuring a prominent performance upgrade, the surface acoustic wave (SAW) device on the multilayer substrate stands out as a strong competitor in fifth-generation (5G) applications. In this paper, harmonics generation in SAW resonators on a 36° YX-LiTaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiC substrate is studied experimentally. Comparative analysis with conventional SAW resonators on a bulk substrate reveals that the layered structure exhibits pronounced harmonic responses induced by transverse modes, which stand as a crucial constraint to its nonlinear performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Frames for Q-Enhancement in Piezoelectric MEMS Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Piezoelectric Micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) resonators have attracted a wide range of interest due to their excellent properties. In this work, an Aluminum Nitride (AlN)-based MEMS resonator with multi-stage frames (MF) is proposed for quality factor (Q) enhancement, where the principle of MF is the effect of mechanical vibration isolation. Using finite element analysis (FEA) method, the proposed MF resonator has less acoustic energy leakage and higher Qanchor compared to the conventional resonators. Measurement results show that the MF resonator has a 1.74-fold unload-Q (Qu) enhancement compared to conventional resonators, suggesting less acoustic energy leakage into the substrates. The MF design is also suitable for high-frequency MEMS resonators with other piezoelectric materials such as Lithium Niobate or Lithium Tantalate.

articleTitle: Analysis of Surface Acoustic Wave Propagation Characteristics on Lead-Free KNN Single Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: This paper simulates the SAW resonator based on three different poling directions Ta-modified KNN (KNNT) single crystal. The date illustrates that the KNN single crystal of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbf{011}]_{\mathbf{c}}$</tex> poling direction is superior to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbf{001}]_{\mathbf{c}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbf{111}]_{\mathbf{c}}$</tex> poling directions in terms of SAW resonator properties. The single-domain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbf{011}]_{\mathbf{c}}-\mathbf{poled}$</tex> KNN-based piezoelectric single crystal exhibits excellent SAW performance. Moreover, the Y-Z KNNT demonstrates high frequency and electromechanical coupling coefficient characteristics, making it highly promising for 5G devices.

articleTitle: Welcome by the Conference Chairs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE MTT-S International Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM)
abstract: Dear IC-MAM'24 Delegates, On behalf of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), represented through its Microwave Theory and Techniques Society (MTT-S), University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC), and our Silver Sponsor Rohde & Schwarz, it is our great pleasure and honor to welcome you to the Second IEEE MTT-S international Conference on Microwave Acoustics & Mechanics (IC-MAM), which is held from May 13 to 15, 2024 in Chengdu, China. Chengdu is known as the happiest city in China, a city of history and gastronomy, and the homeland of giant and lesser pandas.
